welcome_lead: Today you'll weigh sources on Versailles, war guilt and who was really to blame for WWI.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The peace was made at the Paris Peace Conference in 1919.

Wilson wanted his Fourteen Points and a League of Nations. Clemenceau wanted revenge and security against Germany. Lloyd George wanted balance — punish Germany but keep her trading.

The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919.

Article 231 blamed Germany. The army was cut to 100,000 men. Reparations were set at £6.6 billion. Germany lost 13% of land and all colonies. Germans called it a 'diktat'.

walkthroughs.h2: Who was to blame for the war?
walkthroughs.body_html:
Fischer in the 1960s blamed Germany for planning aggressive war.

Others blame the alliance system, Austria-Hungary, or all the great powers stumbling in. Some say the Balkans and ethnic nationalism caused it. Historians still argue today.

mcqs.q: Why did British women get the vote in 1918?
options: Women got the vote as a reward for their work in WWI.
Vesalius invented the microscope.
A combination of pre-war suffragist and suffragette campaigning, women's contribution to WWI, and broader political changes including extending male suffrage.
Emmeline Pankhurst was elected to Parliament and voted it through.
